description: Project-authored evaluation cases written after fixing the initial retrieval thresholds. Labels are intended interpretations, not independent expert annotations. Do not use these cases to claim general language understanding.

cases.text: Release engineer. Stop Friday releases from becoming weekend archaeology. Roll out updates safely and recover the service after failed deployments.
Business analyst. Our spreadsheet tells a different story every Monday. Find patterns in revenue figures and explain the changes to management.
Product designer. Rescue visitors from our maze of menus. Rework navigation and screen layouts after observing where users get stuck.
Technical writer. Translate the engineers' alphabet soup into instructions a first-time user can follow. Make the written steps clear and consistent.
Account executive. Customers have champagne expectations and a lemonade budget. Agree realistic prices and delivery terms with them.
Delivery coordinator. Finance and engineering sometimes speak different languages. Help them agree how to share the workload and resolve disagreements.
Service desk. A caller is upset because an update changed their settings. Hear them out and walk them through restoring the options they need.
Warehouse trainer. Demonstrate how new employees should use the scanner and let them practise until they can complete the process independently.
Quality engineer. Try unusual inputs and repeat yesterday's failure to confirm the patch solves it without breaking existing behaviour.
Policy assistant. Compare evidence from several credible publications and produce a summary of where the findings agree or conflict.
Payroll administrator. Verify employee records against the original forms and catch discrepancies before payments are approved.
Events assistant. Handle urgent requests while maintaining the delivery schedule. Decide which tasks need attention first when deadlines overlap.
Community coordinator. Write updates for our Instagram account and respond to followers' comments in the brand's voice.
Sofware developer. Write application code to support new features and improve the structure of existing modules.
Customer suport specialist. Help customers resolve product difficulties and explain the necessary steps in a friendly way.
This role does not involve writing code or fixing software bugs. You will not be expected to present to clients.

Perks:
Join our writing club and learn presentation skills during optional lunchtime sessions.
How to apply:
Send a polite email explaining why you like our company.
We are a fun and exciting business looking for a rockstar who is amazing at everything.
Professional chair warmer wanted. Must master the art of looking busy while the kettle boils.
We definitely do not need another genius who deletes the database. No programming or database skills are required.
We want someone who looks good in photographs and always wears a smart jacket.
The rain stopped just before lunch and we saw a rainbow over the car park.
